steps: Write down the oven settings: 425F, 25 minutes.
Lower the temperature: 425 minus 25 is 400F, and the time stays 25 minutes.
Or shorten the time: 25 × 0.75 = 18.75, rounded to 19 minutes, at the same 425F.

faqs.answer: 400F for a recipe that bakes at 425F. Take 25F off whatever temperature your recipe gives you, and keep the breast in a single layer.
faqs.question: What temperature do I air fry chicken breast at?

faqs.answer: Either 25 minutes at 400F, or check at about 19 minutes at 425F. A boneless breast that bakes for 25 minutes in the oven converts one way or the other, never both. Pull it at 165F inside.
faqs.question: How long does chicken breast take in the air fryer?

faqs.answer: Just one. Reduce the temperature by 25F and keep the oven time, or keep the oven temperature and check about 25 percent sooner. Doing both undercooks the chicken, because you have taken heat away twice. Either way, the thermometer decides when it is done.
faqs.question: Should I change the temperature and the time, or just one?

faqs.answer: Yes, once, halfway through. The heat comes from above, so the top browns faster. Flipping evens it out and keeps the bottom from staying pale.
faqs.question: Do I flip chicken breast in the air fryer?

faqs.answer: You can, but add about 10 minutes to the converted time and check the temperature twice, in two spots. A frozen breast cooks unevenly, and the centre is the last part to reach 165F.
faqs.question: Can I cook frozen chicken breast in the air fryer?

felicityNote: The flattening step is the one people skip and the one that matters most. An even breast cooks evenly, and evenly is the whole game.

parts.meaning: The air fryer runs hotter than the dial says, because the fan pushes hot air straight onto the food. Dropping 25F keeps the outside from drying out before the centre cooks.
When you lower the temperature, the food still needs the full oven time. The lower heat and the full time balance each other out.
A quarter sooner. Keep the oven temperature and check at three quarters of the oven time. Open the basket then, look, and check the temperature.
The safe internal temperature for chicken, measured in the thickest part with a thermometer.

formula.text: Pick one, never both. Lower the temperature: air fryer temp = oven temp minus 25F, and the time stays the same. Or shorten the time: keep the oven temperature and check at oven time × 0.75. For chicken breast at 425F for 25 minutes: either 400F for 25 minutes, or 425F and check at about 19 minutes.

howToSteps.name: Read the oven settings
howToSteps.text: Find the temperature and time in your recipe. A typical boneless breast bakes at 425F for 25 minutes.

howToSteps.name: Pick one change
howToSteps.text: Pick one change, not both. Either take 25F off the temperature and keep the time, or keep the temperature and check a quarter sooner. 425F for 25 minutes becomes either 400F for 25 minutes or 425F and check at about 19 minutes.

howToSteps.name: Flatten and season
howToSteps.text: Flatten the breast to an even thickness, pat it dry, and season it. Brush on a teaspoon of oil so the outside browns.

howToSteps.name: Cook, flip, and check
howToSteps.text: Cook in a single layer and flip halfway. Pull the breast when the thickest part reads 165F.

title: Oven to Air Fryer: Chicken Breast
tutorial: Chicken breast is the food I convert most, because nearly every chicken recipe on the internet is written for the oven. A boneless breast that bakes at 425F for 25 minutes air fries two ways: 400F for the full 25 minutes, or 425F and check at about 19 minutes. Pick one, not both. That is the whole conversion.

Thickness decides everything. A breast that is thick on one end and thin on the other cooks unevenly in any machine, and the air fryer punishes it more because the heat is so direct. Flatten the thick end with the flat of a knife or a rolling pin until the breast is an even thickness, about three quarters of an inch. Then the converted time means something.

The thermometer is not optional here. Chicken is done at 165F in the thickest part, and no time on any chart changes that. Slide the probe into the centre, away from the pan and away from any bone. If it reads under 165F, give it two more minutes and check again. If it reads 165F, take it out and let it rest for five minutes before slicing, or the juices run out onto the board.

One layer, always. Two breasts side by side with space between them cook in the converted time. Four breasts stacked on top of each other steam in the middle and brown on top, and no conversion fixes that. Cook in two batches if the basket is full. The first batch stays warm under foil while the second cooks.
Some guides say do both, lower the temperature and cut the time. That undercooks, because you have taken heat away twice. Pick one change, not both, and let the thermometer have the last word.
